title: Dissipative framework for subsystem dynamics of noninteracting quantum chains
abstract: When only local observables of a many-body quantum system are of interest, it is desirable to formulate a reduced description within the Hilbert space of the corresponding subsystem, with the remaining degrees of freedom traced out and acting as an environment. Assuming initially uncorrelated states and Gaussian environments, we develop a framework for reconstructing the local dynamical generator of noninteracting quantum chains, with polynomial computational complexity. As an application, we consider two representative models: a bipartitioned Kitaev chain and a Kitaev chain boundary-coupled to a fully connected free-fermion environment. In both models, strong subsystem-environment coupling leads to non-Markovian dynamics characterized by ballistic spreading of the Lindblad dissipator support within the subsystem. On the other hand, weak coupling to a fully connected environment yields predominantly boundary-localized, Markovian dissipation. Our work highlights the implications of subsystem-environment correlations on the generator of local dynamics, beyond the conventional weak-coupling approximations.
summary: This paper presents a general framework to derive the reduced dynamics generator for local observables in noninteracting quantum chains by tracing out the environment. It successfully handles the complexity of subsystem-environment correlations, showing how coupling strength dictates whether the dynamics are Markovian or non-Markovian. This advances the theory of open quantum systems beyond simple weak-coupling approximations.
main_problem: The paper develops a framework to derive a reduced description for local observables of a many-body quantum system by tracing out the environment, particularly for noninteracting quantum chains.
main_result: The framework successfully reconstructs the time-local dynamical generator for noninteracting chains with polynomial complexity, characterizing how subsystem-environment correlations affect local dynamics beyond weak-coupling approximations.
method: The approach uses open quantum systems theory, assuming Gaussian environments and initially uncorrelated states to derive the generator $\mathcal{L}_t$ governing the subsystem evolution.
model_or_system: The study focuses on noninteracting quantum chains (e.g., Kitaev chain), treating the total system as partitioned into a subsystem (S) and an environment (E). Dynamics are analyzed via the evolution of the correlation matrix $\Theta_t$.
key_observables: Reduced density operators ($ho_S(t)$), correlation matrix ($\Theta_t$), and non-Markovianity measures like the Rivas-Huelga-Plenio (RHP) and Breuer-Laine-Piilo (BLP) measures.
important_parameters: Coupling strength, inverse temperature ($ eta$), and the structure of the environment (e.g., fully connected free-fermion environment).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on assuming initially uncorrelated states ($\chi_0 = 0$) and Gaussian environments ($ho_{E0}$), which allows for the reconstruction of the generator with polynomial complexity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of non-Markovianity measures and the time evolution of correlation matrix components ($\alpha(t), \Gamma_1(t), \Gamma_2(t)$) under varying coupling strengths and temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper builds the framework by defining the reduced dynamics generator, applying it to specific models like the Kitaev chain, and analyzing the resulting non-Markovian dynamics using established measures.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, computationally tractable method to study non-Markovian dynamics in complex quantum systems by systematically handling the environment coupling, which is crucial for understanding realistic open quantum systems.

FIG. 2. Time evolution of α(t), Γ1(t) and Γ2(t) for a single-site sys- tem, g ∈{0.5, 1, 2} (top to bottom) and β ∈{0, 1} (left to right). FIG. 3. Time evolution of the coupling amplitudes {Γξ,σ(t), ξ = 1, 2, σ = ±} for l ∈{2, 4, 8}, L = 200, g ∈{0.5, 1, 2} (top to bot- tom) and β ∈{0, 1} (left to right), shown on a semi-log scale. For all cases considered, we observe a transient regime with exponentially growing rates, and an approach to stationarity for t ≳l/2vmax.

FIG. 6. Profiles of the creation weights |aξ,+ j | in the Lindblad oper- ators at time t = 12 for l = 8, L = 400, g = 1, β = 0 (left) and β = 1 (right). After the transient, ballistically spreading Lindblad operators have reached half of the subsystem, they hybridize and de- localize over all the l sites. (a) For β = 0, the rates Γξ,σ at ξ = 1, 2 are degenerate and one can choose the corresponding Lindblad oper- ators for ξ = 1, 2 to be symmetric with respect to the middle of the chain. (b) For β > 0, rates Γξ,σ at ξ = 1, 2 are not degenerate and the associated Lindblad operators are distinct.

FIG. 4. Profiles of the creation weights |aξ,σ j | at times t ∈{2, 4, 8} for l = 32, L = 400, g = 1, β = 0. The profiles of the Lindblad operators are symmetric, and spread ballistically from the edges to the bulk over time. The annihilation amplitudes |bξ,σ j | are omitted as they show the same weights.
